newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco union says Sudbury workers to strike.
newsitem.headline: Inco union says Sudbury workers to strike.

text.p: The union representing 4670 workers at Inco Ltd's Sudbury operations said on Monday that members voted 60.4 percent to reject a tentative contract agreement.
As a result, unionized workers at Sudbury will be on strike effective midnight Monday, union officials said.
"We're on strike at 1201 (EDT)," Gary Patterson, vice-president of local 6500 of the United Steelworkers of America, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Inco and union negotiators reached a tentative agreement on Friday, a day before workers had been scheduled to strike at midnight on Saturday.
But in Monday's ratification vote, the three-year contract offer was rejected by 2,638 of the 4,397 workers who voted.
The contract affects unionized workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne, Ontario.
Results from the vote taken by workers at Port Colborne were not immediately available, but union officials said the Sudbury strike would affect those operations.

According to Inco's production plan for the current fiscal year, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper, and about four million pounds of cobalt.
Patterson said the union had not yet talked to the company about resuming negotiations.
"I think we'll call and if they want to talk to us, okay. If not, then we'll sit and wait," he said.

Asked why the membership rejected the offer, Patterson said: "There were a number of things that were missing. There was nothing in it for the younger members from their perspective. We'll have to gather our thoughts tommorrow," he said.
Inco officials were unavailable for comment.
